newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Beirut to list on Beirut Stock Exchange.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Beirut to list on Beirut Stock Exchange.

text.p: Bank of Beirut plans to list its shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange, possibly by the end of March, a source close to the bank said on Friday.
"Bank of Beirut will list 30 percent of its shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange within two months; maybe by the end of March," the source told Reuters.
"Although projected demand for the shares from the Gulf Arab investors is high, strong demand from the local market is also expected," the source added.

Two other banks have already listed 30 percent of their shares since December 30 -- Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce and Banque Audi -- and both have been star performers on the largely lacklustre market.

At least one other bank, Byblos Bank, is expected to list on the exchange in March. A law passed last year allows banks to list and trade up to 30 percent of their shares on the stock market without prior permission from the central bank.
Dealers say bank listings will invigorate the bourse which has been quiet ever since it reopened in January 1996 after having been shut down at the height of the 1975-90 civil war.
BLC and Audi closed at $12 and $16.125 respectively on Friday from $11.25 and $15 when they first began trading on December 30 and January 20.
According to Bank of Beirut's unaudited 1996 financial results, net income rose to 7.99 billion Lebanese pounds from 4.31 billion in 1995 and its assets rose to 717.8 billion pounds from 452 billion.
Bank of Beirut ranked 17th among Lebanon's 82 banks in size of customer deposits in 1995.

According to the Almanac of Lebanese banks, Bank of Beirut is owned by nine Lebanese investors, Saudi Prince Mohammad Bin al-Saoud and Luxembourg-based holding company International Century Corporation.
